title: Benchmark monitoring dashboards + guardrails (canary gating) for public latency/$ runs
creator: Neha Kapoor
project: Latency per Dollar Public Benchmark Report
description:
Context
- We’re running multi-region benchmark windows for the public “latency per dollar” report. These runs are intentionally high-load (concurrency sweeps) and must not regress production SLOs.
- We need: (1) region-specific dashboards to validate run health and capture screenshots/receipts, (2) alerting that pages the on-call if we’re impacting production or collecting invalid data, and (3) automatic canary gating that pauses/stops the benchmark runner when production health degrades.

Goals
1) Prevent benchmark activity from impacting production traffic (or stop it quickly if it does).
2) Ensure benchmark artifacts are defensible (clear health signals, run markers, and “abort” events recorded).
3) Make it easy for SRE + Perf/Evals to run windows consistently across regions.

Non-goals
- Building new customer-facing product observability features.
- Publishing raw logs/traces.

Deliverables
A) Dashboards (per region)
- “Benchmark Window Overview” dashboard with:
  - API p50/p95/p99 latency for benchmark routes and overall (split by region)
  - 5xx rate, timeouts, and saturation signals (queue depth / pending batches)
  - GPU utilization + memory, KV cache pressure, OOM/evictions
  - Request volume by route + benchmark runner tag
  - Spot capacity / node health indicators (node churn, restarts)
  - Cost/metering sanity: tokens/s and $/hr (coarse) for the pool
- Required: annotations/markers for benchmark windows so screenshots are unambiguous.

B) Alerts
- Page (SRE on-call) when any of the following triggers while a benchmark window flag is active:
  - Production p95 latency breach (route-group: chat + embeddings) sustained 5 min
  - Error rate (5xx + timeouts) > threshold sustained 3 min
  - GPU saturation > threshold sustained 10 min AND queue depth rising
  - Node instability (restarts) above threshold during window
- Non-paging notifications to #eng-sre and #eng-ml for “data validity” issues:
  - High variance indicator (run-to-run p95 drift) beyond allowed band
  - Metering anomaly: token throughput drops while cost attribution stays constant

C) Canary gating (automatic stop)
- Integrate perf-canary guardrails so benchmark runner pauses/stops when:
  - any paging alert would fire, OR
  - region health check endpoint returns “degraded”, OR
  - headroom guard fails (min available GPU headroom for production pool)
- Behavior:
  - Phase 1: pause benchmark traffic (stop scheduling new benchmark jobs)
  - Phase 2: if health does not recover within N minutes, abort window and mark run as “invalidated-by-guardrail” in artifacts
  - Always emit an audit trail (timestamp, trigger condition, region, who acknowledged)

Implementation notes
- Benchmark traffic is tagged via headers and routed through the benchmark runner; all dashboards/alerts must be filterable by this tag.
- Add a “benchmark_window=true” flag in region runner orchestration (ENG-2860) to prevent guardrails from paging outside scheduled windows.
- Ensure guardrails don’t mask real incidents: they should still page if production is impacted; we’re gating the benchmark runner, not suppressing production alerts.

Links
- Observability dashboards PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-904-benchmark-dashboards.json
- Guardrails PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-266-benchmark-window-guardrails.json
- Region orchestration PR (runner tags/flags): sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-147-region-runner-orchestration.json
- Capacity windows plan (reference): sources/confluence/eng-sre/capacity-planning/benchmark-run-capacity-window-plan.json

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Dashboards exist for NA/EU/APAC regions and include window annotations + benchmark runner filters.
- [x] Paging alerts wired to on-call only when benchmark_window=true AND impact thresholds exceeded.
- [x] Canary gating pauses benchmark scheduling within 60s of a trigger and records an abort marker.
- [x] Runbook section added: how to validate health pre-run, what to monitor during run, and how to respond to a guardrail abort.
- [x] SRE sign-off recorded in ticket comments before report launch.
comments:
2025-02-03 — Neha Kapoor (creator)
Created for launch readiness. We need a single owner for the guardrail + dashboard pieces; prior ad-hoc monitoring won’t scale across regions. Please treat this as a hard dependency for public benchmark credibility and production safety.

Requested reviewers: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Claire Dubois (Perf/Evals).

Target: land by end of week so we can run at least one full rehearsal window with alerts enabled.

2025-02-04 — Keiko Yamamoto (assignee)
Plan:
1) Dashboards/alerts in observability-pack (Grafana) with a consistent region variable + benchmark_runner tag.
2) perf-canary: add a “benchmark window guard” that subscribes to health signals and calls back into benchmark-lab to pause/abort.
3) Add artifact marker: write a small JSON line into the run directory when guardrails fire.

Open question for SRE: what thresholds do we use for “production p95 breach” during windows? Should we key off existing SLO burn alerts, or define a tighter benchmark-specific threshold?

2025-02-05 — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Use existing SLO alert thresholds as the paging source of truth; don’t invent new “benchmark-only” latency numbers unless we have strong justification.

Two asks:
- Make sure benchmark_window=true gates the paging-to-benchmark-runner behavior, but *does not* silence the production paging path.
- Add a clear “pre-flight checklist” panel: current error rate, p95, GPU headroom, node restart rate; if any are already abnormal, the run should not start.

Also: ensure the annotations include window start/stop, and any guardrail abort events.

2025-02-07 — Keiko Yamamoto
Draft dashboards are up in observability-pack PR-904. Includes:
- Window annotations (start/stop) and a separate annotation stream for guardrail abort events.
- Filters: region, model, route-group (chat/embeddings), benchmark_runner=true.
- Panels requested by SRE + Perf/Evals.

Next: wire alerts and perf-canary integration. Waiting on final naming for the benchmark_window flag from ENG-2860 (runner orchestration).

2025-02-08 — Claire Dubois (Perf/Evals)
Dashboards look good. One request: add a panel that overlays “bench request p95 latency” vs “overall p95 latency” so we can spot if the runner is causing cross-tenant interference. We’ve been burned by only looking at benchmark-tagged latency before.

Also: please ensure abort markers flow into the artifacts so QC can flag those runs automatically.

2025-02-11 — Keiko Yamamoto
Implemented the overlay panel Claire requested.

perf-canary PR-266 is up with:
- BenchmarkWindowGuard: subscribes to existing SLO alert state + a lightweight /healthz/degraded endpoint.
- Actions: pause scheduling new benchmark jobs, then abort after 5 minutes if not recovered.
- Writes guardrail_abort.json into the run artifact path (region/model/run_id).

Needs review from SRE re: paging conditions and whether we should abort immediately on error spikes vs “pause first”.

2025-02-12 — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Reviewed perf-canary PR. Pause-first behavior is correct; immediate abort can create confusing partial artifacts and makes post-mortems harder.

Requested changes:
- Reduce pause detection latency: poll interval from 60s -> 15s while benchmark_window=true.
- Add a hard stop if production 5xx exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive minutes (no 5-minute grace).
- Ensure the guard records which trigger fired (latency, 5xx, saturation, node churn).

Once those land, I’m good to approve.

2025-02-14 — Keiko Yamamoto
Addressed SRE asks:
- Poll interval now 15s during active window.
- Added immediate abort path for sustained 5xx (3 min).
- Abort record includes trigger_type + trigger_source + timestamps.

Also coordinated with ENG-2860 to standardize benchmark_window flag name and propagation.

Requesting re-review on PR-266.

2025-02-15 — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Approved. Please make sure the runbook references:
- where to see guardrail abort annotations
- where the artifact marker lives
- who to page if the guard is firing repeatedly (capacity vs runtime regression)

With that: SRE sign-off granted for launch usage.

2025-02-18 — Keiko Yamamoto
Runbook text added to the benchmark execution doc and linked from the dashboard.

Rehearsal run in eu-west completed; guardrails did not fire. Confirmed we get both window annotations and an abort annotation (tested via forced degraded health check).

2025-02-20 — Neha Kapoor
Marking Done. This is now part of the required launch checklist: benchmark windows cannot proceed without dashboards live + guardrails enabled + SRE on-call aware of the scheduled window.
